description.p: Kopuz is a fast, modern music player built with Rust and the Dioxus framework. It scans your local music folders and organizes them into a browsable library by artist and album. Features include full playback controls, an immersive fullscreen player, dynamic theming, and system media integration. And also We have Jellyfin server integration. To listen to your music from your Jellyfin server.
Designed for performance and simplicity.

Android builds and ships again, with an arm64 APK, a signed release job, an F-Droid recipe, and a phone-sized interface with swipe gestures, notification shuffle and repeat, and an AMOLED theme. Two new sources arrive: Apple Music, with catalog and library browsing, downloads, word-timed lyrics and Widevine playback through a CDM borrowed from an installed browser, and Nextcloud over WebDAV, which reads the library from the folder tree, probes durations from file headers, and takes per-server library folders. Lyrics gain depth-of-field blur, instrumental breaks, a permanently centered active line, and a manual or automatic offset. Remote tracks start faster on pooled connections with window prefetching, radio uses server-side sonic similarity where an OpenSubsonic server offers it, macOS gains a Homebrew cask, and the app identity finished its move to moe.kopuz.kopuz, migrating existing data on first launch. Offline downloads and deletions no longer trust remote or persisted paths.

Settings move out of the database into a hand-editable settings.toml, with drop-in and environment overrides and support for declarative management through hjem. Word-timed lyrics now fill glyph by glyph, remote audio streams over HTTP ranges with a visible buffer, and Subsonic servers that offer a server-side song radio queue drive the radio. The Flatpak builds from source under the moe.kopuz.kopuz app id with host spawn made opt-in, settings show the version and build commit, and fixes cover CD-layout scroll performance, playlist scrolling and covers, RTL transport controls, light-mode sidebar text, and app-wide space play/pause.

Playlists gain radio: YouTube Music can start a mix from a playlist, and the button shows up wherever a source supports it, with YouTube liked music now listed as a playlist of its own. Matugen and pywal palettes can drive the theme live, the settings screen is reorganized with a choice of layouts, and Spotify playback works in Helium. Album lists show real metadata track numbers, favorites can be filtered by search, the fullscreen player gets favorite and track actions, and releases now ship AppImage, DEB, RPM, DMG, EXE and MSI packages from one workflow.

Spotify joins as a streaming backend, built on the public Web API: your saved tracks, albums and playlists, a Discover page, search and scrobbling, with playback through Spotify's Web Playback SDK or any Spotify Connect device you own. Cover reference encoding is centralized in one place, which fixed Subsonic playlist tracks being written with Jellyfin album ids and cover refs being pasted into image tag parameters. Subsonic playlists now use their own cover art, the downloader gains an Opus format, album release years are read from more tag fields, and local files scrobble to Libre.fm again.

Isolated local libraries: create named local libraries with their own folders and switch between them like any media server. Library scans are much faster — metadata parsing is parallelized, artwork is skipped in the foreground and indexed in the background one track per album, and same-titled albums by different artists no longer collide. Local artwork is served at the size each view renders it, with an optional cap for keeping even the large views small. The settings page is revised with collapsible sections, tighter rows, and custom keyboard-navigable dropdowns.

A 10-band equalizer, a quick search overlay, custom UI fonts, a reworked fullscreen view with cover art backgrounds, an expanded radio experience with radio-browser.info search and ICY now-playing metadata, Helium browser support for sign-in, a Swedish locale, and media server reachability checks.

Player engine rewrite for more reliable playback, multi-priority sorting across album, library, and artist views, configurable output sample rate, offline scrobbling support, and Discord presence reconnection when Discord starts late or restarts.

Native botguard for YouTube Music, more reliable ListenBrainz scrobbling with retries, smoother scrolling with data queries moved off the UI thread, grouped settings sections, and Flatpak browser support.
